summary: Full QA pass on WP-012. Build verified (0 warnings, 0 errors). All 5 acceptance criteria confirmed.
AC-1 (round-trip): add/list/remove correctly persists and retrieves folders via InMemorySpdbConfigRepository seam. No-op remove for unknown id verified.
AC-2 (monotonic counter): three sequential adds yield strictly increasing ids; first id starts at 1.
AC-3 (remove-then-add id ordering): counter never regresses after remove; new id > all previously issued ids.

AC-4 (LIKE underscore escaping): BuildLikePrefix correctly escapes \ (backslash), % (percent), _ (underscore) in correct order. Functional simulation on Windows confirms C:\\Users\\test\_folder\\% for path C:\Users\test_folder.
AC-5 (all tests pass): 11/11 new tests pass; full regression: 232 passed, 4 pre-existing skipped, 0 failed.

metrics.test_coverage: 11 new unit tests: 3 round-trip (AC-1), 2 counter monotonicity (AC-2), 1 remove-then-add (AC-3), 5 BuildLikePrefix escaping (AC-4)

comments.note: BuildLikePrefix escape order verified: backslash escaped first (\ \\), then % (\%), then _ (\_). This is the correct order — reversing would double-escape the escape character itself. Functional simulation on Windows confirms output C:\\Users\\test\_folder\\% for input C:\Users\test_folder.

SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository: the internal ISpdbConfigRepository seam correctly skips the DB-level cascade delete (movies_filenames and movies orphan cleanup) since that logic requires a live Dapper/MySQL connection. Unit tests cover the folder list management logic only; cascade semantics remain covered by VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests integration tests.

RemoveAsync on a folder path with a trailing directory separator (e.g., C:\Movies\) would produce a double-separator in the LIKE pattern (C:\\Movies\\\\%). Not exercised by current tests and unlikely in practice, but worth noting for completeness.

summary: Code review PASS. WP-012 reviewed: SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository.cs (modified) and SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepositoryUnitTests.cs (new).

The internal test seam constructor is pragmatically appropriate given the documented constraint that the production path requires a shared IDbTransaction which ISpdbConfigRepository cannot provide. The seam is clearly marked internal, well-documented, and does not alter production behavior.
BuildLikePrefix escape order (backslash first, then %, then _) is correct. The method is correctly marked internal static for testability.

One medium-priority maintainability note: the nullable _connectionFactory? / _configRepository? fields plus null-forgiving operators rely on constructor-invariant correctness rather than the type system. Not a blocking issue but noted for future awareness.

0 Blocking findings. 0 Fix-Forward changes. All 5 acceptance criteria met.

comments.note: SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository.cs: The internal test seam constructor is a reasonable pragmatic choice given the documented constraint — IDbConnectionFactory is used directly in production because ISpdbConfigRepository creates a new connection per call and cannot share a transaction. The XML doc on the internal constructor clearly states this and documents the cascade-delete skip. No Blocking issue.

SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository.cs: The two nullable fields _connectionFactory? and _configRepository? combined with the null-forgiving operator (_connectionFactory!) in the production path is a design smell. Correctness relies on a constructor-enforced invariant rather than the type system. A future developer could add a third constructor that sets neither field and not receive any compile-time warning before hitting a NullReferenceException at runtime. This is a medium-priority maintainability concern but not a logic bug in the current code.

SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository.cs: AddViaConfigRepositoryAsync and RemoveViaConfigRepositoryAsync duplicate the counter-read-increment-write and list-read-modify-write logic from the Dapper path. The Developer acknowledged this debt. If the ID allocation semantics ever change, both paths must be updated in sync. Consider extracting a shared FolderStateManager value object in a future refactor to eliminate the duplication.

BuildLikePrefix: The backslash-first escape order is correct and the logic is clean. On Windows, the directory separator is \ which is also the LIKE escape character — the method correctly escapes it as \\\\ (four chars: two for C# string literal, two for the actual LIKE pattern). The QA escape-order verification confirms this is functionally correct.

[documentation-forward] SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository.cs: Consider adding a brief class-level remark noting the two-field null invariant — that exactly one of _connectionFactory and _configRepository is non-null at runtime, determined by which constructor was used. This would help future developers understand the nullable field declarations and the null-forgiving operators without needing to read the implementation pipeline history.
